meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty-five minutes before a client call, so let's not waste them. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him or to me first?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Owen found out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. What is the zero based on, Hale?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing down November 2. A student answering "like, being stuck" to one question in a hallway is an impression, Hale. Where is the note you made that day? Show me.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

You still haven't shown me the note from November 2. People change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's called revising. Put the October 15 outline on the table next to the essay, and then we'll talk.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

You're offering a rewrite while the zero stays on the gradebook, and your written promise arrives on Friday, after Thursday. I want the terms in writing before Thursday, the zero off the gradebook until then, and the outline and the November 2 note on the table. Otherwise I'm going to the principal.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, the terms in writing before Thursday, and the outline and your November 2 note in front of me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: the principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, wanting the zero withdrawn, the terms in writing before Thursday and your documents shown, or she goes to the principal.
What moved her: owning the zero before the call home in one sentence gave a small sign of ground, and naming November 2 and the October 15 outline gave her specifics, though she saw no paper.
What cost ground: offering the rewrite before showing any document, with the zero still in place and your written promise arriving after the rewrite, because it skipped the evidence she had asked for twice.
Try next time: when she asks to see the November 2 note, put it in front of her before you mention any rewrite.
